video_title: FOMO Founder Defends Memecoins + AMC vs Robinhood - The Chopping Block
gist: FOMO co-founder Paul argues the blockchain is the best substrate ever built for a financial social graph and that his app is already the dominant distribution channel on Robinhood's chain (94k active wallets vs 30k for the number-two app, with Robinhood chain earning roughly $42M in about 70 days), while the Dragonfly and Gauntlet hosts push back that the memecoin production function reliably shreds retail capital. The panel then dissects AMC's public fight with Robinhood over unauthorized stock tokenization and closes on the OpenAI-versus-Anthropic credit war over a claimed Navier-Stokes proof.

insights.claim: FOMO's founding thesis is that onchain trading is the biggest change to financial markets since trading was computerized in the 1970s, and that the winning use cases are global distribution and a transparent social graph rather than skeuomorphic ports of Web2 apps onto a chain.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: If distribution and social discovery are the real onchain primitives, value accrues to consumer front-ends and identity layers rather than to yet another decentralized-Twitter or infrastructure play.
insights.quote: onchain is the largest revolution in the financial industry since trading was computerized for the first time in the 1970s and everyone's trying to build these skumorphic applications

insights.claim: A public ledger is structurally superior to a bank-and-API stack for building a social trading network, because every transaction already exists and the only missing layer is identity and presentation, whereas a traditional broker would need separate accounts and exposed APIs per user.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: This is the clearest argument for why a crypto-native social trading app can ship features that eToro or Webull structurally cannot, and it is testable by watching whether equities social trading migrates onchain.
insights.quote: the underlying architecture of the blockchain is the best architecture ever created for a social graph because it's just there and all you have to do is just create something around it

insights.claim: Previous social trading products such as eToro and Webull failed because optional privacy creates a game-theoretic equilibrium where everyone goes private and only wins get posted, producing confirmation bias and mistrust; mandatory full transparency of every trade is the structural fix.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: The 'it has been tried before' objection to social trading is answered by a design change, not a marketing change, which is the kind of distinction that separates a repeat failure from a category winner.
insights.quote: the game theoretical optimal thing if you have a private mode is to be private and everyone else to be public, right? So then everyone goes private.

insights.claim: FOMO deliberately refuses to build copy trading and instead pays creator rewards for attributed trades, having already distributed $2.5 million, while surfacing average hold time as a headline statistic to push users toward longer holds and published theses.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: A creator-rewards flywheel that pays for attributed volume is a real revenue-sharing model to watch; it also makes influencer attention a measurable, monetizable input rather than a free externality.
insights.quote: we hate the idea of copy trading and we've never built that because the whole point of FOMO is that you get full information and then you can learn by doing

insights.claim: FOMO's incentive structure is deliberately opposed to a launchpad's, because a launchpad earns by minting coins as fast as possible while FOMO earns by keeping traders solvent and holding longer.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: Business-model incentives are the best predictor of which crypto consumer apps degrade their users, and this framing gives a way to screen the sector.
insights.quote: if you're tied to a launchpad, right, your incentive is to create coins as fast as possible because that's how you earn money

insights.claim: Teams including Pawns, Solana, LayerZero and Monad are now holding treasury supply on FOMO and pushing updates as notifications to their token holders, which the founder frames as the highest-intent distribution channel ever created for a financial product and eventually a channel for public company CEOs to reach shareholders in real time.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: A direct issuer-to-holder notification channel is a genuinely new distribution asset; if it migrates to equities it competes with investor relations, brokerages, and financial media all at once.
insights.quote: It's the highest intent distribution channel that's ever existed for a financial product cuz you're have a direct line of communication with the exact people that's holding your financial asset

insights.claim: Forced onchain transparency is already functioning as a reputation-enforcement mechanism, with users visibly posting a thesis and dumping the position seconds later, and some traders deleting their accounts after being socially exposed.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra, Gauntlet
insights.so_what: A platform that automatically scores influencer credibility devalues paid promotion and creates a persistent, tradeable reputation layer over crypto attention markets.
insights.quote: you'll see someone who's like, "Here's why I bought this 300K in market cap coin and here's my thesis and then like 3 seconds later you get another notification that's like they sold everything their thesis.

insights.claim: In an environment where LLMs commoditize opinion, what a person actually holds becomes the only credible signal of belief, which is the basis for a claim that top traders become the next celebrity class.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: If verified position disclosure becomes the scarce credibility asset, platforms that own the proof layer capture the attention economy that currently sits on Twitter and YouTube.
insights.quote: in the world of AI where it's really easy to have opinion and that's commoditized because you just talk to an LLM. What you're holding is what your actual belief is.

insights.claim: Roughly 70% or more of Robinhood chain's users are estimated to have arrived via FOMO, inverting the 2024-era pattern where a chain brought users to wallets and apps.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra, Gauntlet
insights.so_what: If applications now supply chains with users rather than the reverse, chain token valuations built on assumed organic demand are actually leveraged bets on a handful of front-ends.
insights.quote: I I don't know exactly the stats, but it it was something like 70% plus of Robin Hood users came from FOMO.

insights.claim: FOMO reports 94,000 active wallets on Robinhood chain versus 30,000 for the second-largest application on that chain, roughly three times the next competitor.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: Extreme app-level concentration on a new chain means the chain's fee revenue is hostage to a single third-party application's retention.
insights.quote: FOMO had 94,000 active wallets on Robin Hood chain. The second largest app had 30,000, right?

insights.claim: Robinhood chain has generated roughly $42 million in chain revenue in about 70 days of operation, around $600,000 per day with roughly 90% going to Robinhood, a level material even at the corporate level for a company of Robinhood's size.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: A new, high-margin revenue line running at roughly $220M annualized is a concrete input to Robinhood's earnings model and a reason to watch chain activity as an equity signal.
insights.quote: They've made about 42 million in chain revenue. So enormous amount of fees, 600k a day, 90% of that going to Robin Hood.

insights.claim: Robinhood chain's fee revenue is congestion rent rather than durable pricing power, since fees are high only because demand exceeds available block space.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Congestion-derived revenue collapses when either activity falls or capacity expands, so it should be discounted heavily rather than extrapolated.
insights.quote: That kind of revenue is really coming from congestion effectively. Like that's what that's why the fees are so high is because there's so much demand and there's only so much block space.

insights.claim: If most buying flow is intermediated by chain-agnostic apps, the market should begin implicitly load-balancing new token launches across Base, Solana, Ethereum and others, shifting value capture from chains toward applications.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: This is the central bear case for chain-token value accrual in a front-end-dominated market and is directly observable in launch-venue share data.
insights.quote: almost you can just start not you but sort of the market itself can start to load balance uh the different coins launching across different chains.

insights.claim: The load-balancing thesis is idealistic because narrative dominates venue choice: traders crowd into the same coins on the same days, and an attention asset paired with a real-world asset narratively belongs on Robinhood chain regardless of where the buyers actually are.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: Narrative stickiness means chain-level revenue concentration can persist longer than a pure economics model predicts, which matters for anyone shorting chain fee capture.
insights.quote: I think it's a bit idealistic because people just want to trade the same coins I feel like on the same days and it's whatever the narrative is running.

insights.claim: Cross-chain gasless trading did not exist a year ago, and FOMO treats liquidity aggregation and solver routing improvements as the unsolved problem it intends to convert into a competitive moat.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: Execution quality across chains, not UI, is where a consumer trading app's defensibility actually sits, and it is the piece least visible to users.
insights.quote: crosschain trading is a very new thing. Like this thing didn't even exist 6 months to a year ago

insights.claim: Chain abstraction in FOMO is complete enough that an experienced crypto investor deposited funds available in about three seconds and spent a weekend buying copycat tokens without knowing whether he was on Robinhood chain or Solana.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra, Gauntlet
insights.so_what: When users cannot tell which chain they are on, chain-level brand and token demand lose their retail anchor, reinforcing the app-captures-value case.
insights.quote: I didn't think about what chain I was using at all in fact there were about 50 50% of the time I was buying copycat Hunter Biden coins I uh I thought I was buying them on Robin Hane I was buying from Salana.

insights.claim: The most damaging part of the memecoin economy is not trading existing coins like Doge but the memecoin production function of constant new launches, where a supply chain of middlemen extracts value and buyers reliably lose money.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Separating secondary-market memecoin trading from primary issuance is the analytic distinction that determines which parts of this sector face regulatory and reputational risk.
insights.quote: I think the phenomenon that I find to be most delletterious are generally speaking like the memecoin production function. I think that's where most of the value gets shredded

insights.claim: Roughly 5% of memecoin buyers are systematic players who profit while the other 95% lose money, which makes the category a negative-sum activity for nearly all participants regardless of tooling quality.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: A stated 95% loss rate sets the ceiling on how large a sustainable retail memecoin user base can be and puts a clock on any business dependent on new-user inflow.
insights.quote: The other 95% of people who are buying memecoins are losing money.

insights.claim: Not all forms of gambling are equally harmful, and by analogy to lotteries being far worse than roulette, memecoins paired to stock tokens in the prior week's structures were almost comically designed so that every buyer lost.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Harm gradients within speculative products are where regulators eventually draw lines, so the worst-designed structures are the leading indicators of intervention.
insights.quote: Everybody buying these was losing money because they were just obviously a horrible design and they were almost like comically designed to lose money.

insights.claim: Customer churn is the governing metric for any social trading, casino or mobile game business, because an app that lets users blow their entire bankroll cannot refill its funnel fast enough and will have a short half-life.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Retention, not volume, is the diligence question for consumer crypto trading apps, and a platform that survives users' losses is doing something structurally different from a launchpad.
insights.quote: customer churn is the most important metric to keep an eye on. And if you are just allowing your customers to just incinerate themselves by making bad decisions, your business is going to flame out very quickly.

insights.claim: The social component of trading is durable and intrinsic rather than a memecoin-specific fad, having migrated from Twitter and group chats into apps like FOMO, and is expected to extend to ordinary tokens, equities and other productive assets.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: If social trading is the durable layer and memecoins merely its first expression, the investable asset is the social graph, not the current asset class flowing through it.
insights.quote: the social aspect of trading is very deeply ingrained and once upon a time that social graph was on Twitter or it was in group chats. Now it's clearly extending into FOMO

insights.claim: Onchain trading is experienced by at least some sophisticated participants as a video game rather than as investing, with the reward being social status from spotting a trend first rather than the profit itself.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra, Gauntlet
insights.so_what: Entertainment-motivated flow is far less price-sensitive and far more attention-driven than investment flow, which changes how one models volume persistence in a drawdown.
insights.quote: it was like playing a video game. So it's like it was like more like playing a video game than like trading.

insights.claim: The launchpad market has fragmented from Pump.fun dominance into a three-way fight, with Pawns on Robinhood chain now ranking number one by revenue, Stomp.fund on Solana number two, and Pump third.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Pump losing the revenue crown after long dominance is a concrete competitive datapoint for anyone holding launchpad tokens or modeling Solana application fees.
insights.quote: as of yesterday, they were the number one launchpad by revenue. Stomp fund was the number two by revenue and then Pump was number three, which is surprising given that Pump historically has been the king.

insights.claim: Nobody actually wants a fair launch because the entire product is the chance to get in early for outsized upside, which guarantees a perpetual cycle of new launchpads and new metas rather than convergence on one venue.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: Structural demand for unfair early access means launchpad market share is inherently unstable, so incumbency in this category should be valued at a low multiple.
insights.quote: no one really wants a fair launch because then like the whole point is that you're buying and having this chance to get in early and see this tremendous upside

insights.claim: An SEC allowance for distributing business equity through a token launch up to roughly $5 million opens a path to Kickstarter-style projects raising with a token and a launchpad team supporting the build, moving issuance beyond cats and dogs toward utility and real-world-event assets.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: A small-dollar exempt token equity path would legitimize launchpads as capital formation infrastructure, which is a much larger addressable market than meme issuance.
insights.quote: the SEC re recently put out this thing where it's like you can give out like I think it's equity in a business through a token launch if it's up to $5 million

insights.claim: Hunter Biden has announced a memecoin called laptop launching September 9th on Base, with airdrops promised to people who lost money on the Trump token, to his Substack subscribers and to Channel 5 subscribers, and with a supply burn mechanism tied to outcomes such as Democrats winning the midterms or Bitcoin reaching 100K.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: A politically mirrored celeb coin with conditional burns is a template other political figures can copy, and its post-launch performance is a clean test of whether celeb-coin demand has decayed.
insights.quote: he's launching this memecoin called laptop on September 9th on base.

insights.claim: Channel 5 publicly disavowed the laptop token airdrop and said it did not know how its subscriber email list was obtained, making the distribution itself a reputational and possibly legal liability rather than a marketing asset.
insights.speaker: co-host
insights.so_what: Unauthorized use of third-party subscriber lists for airdrop targeting is a new compliance surface that could draw regulatory attention faster than the token design itself.
insights.quote: channel 5 put those statements like don't you know I don't know how they got our email list we don't endorse this this memecoin

insights.claim: Some laptop-token clones were paired with short US Treasury bond ETF tokens so that memecoin buyers received LP fees denominated in the short-bond token, which is structurally the same as familiar crypto rebasing designs but feels materially different because the underlying is a real-world asset.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra, Gauntlet
insights.so_what: Memecoin structures are now embedding real fixed-income exposure as a reward leg, quietly building retail distribution for tokenized Treasuries through a speculative wrapper.
insights.quote: some of the laptop clones were pairing with like short US bond ETFs. So you like buy laptop and you get airdrop LP fees in short US bond token.

insights.claim: Most real-world-asset volume on chains running stock-token pairings comes from memecoin-paired RWA trading rather than trading of the RWAs themselves, meaning chains are using memecoins as a customer-acquisition funnel for tokenized real assets.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: Headline RWA volume metrics on these chains overstate genuine tokenized-asset adoption and should be decomposed before being used as evidence of institutional traction.
insights.quote: most of the volumes on RWA on these chains is actually through the memecoins paired RWA, not actually trading of the RWA themselves

insights.claim: Memecoins paired with a company's stock token can function as a community-building funnel for that company in the GameStop mold, and public company CEOs have already joined FOMO to watch and interact with holders of coins tied to their names.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: If issuers start engaging rather than resisting, memecoin communities become a new and unregulated channel of retail shareholder mobilization with real governance consequences.
insights.quote: My take is that meme coins with stock tokens I think are great communitybuilding aspects for these companies, right? You saw what happened with GameStop, right?

insights.claim: The community a company acquires through memecoin pairing turns hostile in the second half of the cycle, exposing executives to rug-pull-grade online abuse that even a CEO whose stock is down 80% would never receive, which makes issuer engagement a bad risk trade.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Executive reputational risk from token association is asymmetric and back-loaded, which argues that any issuer flirting with pairings is underpricing its downside.
insights.quote: People don't go after, you know, random CEOs whose stock is down like 80% and just be like, "You [ __ ] scammer, you blah blah blah." People will absolutely do that for just like a $10 million memecoin rug pull.

insights.claim: Celebrity tokens are consistently the worst-performing and worst-designed category within the memecoin universe, a pattern the panel says holds across Trump, Melania, Kanye and Iggy Azalea coins.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: A consistently identifiable worst-in-class category is a straightforward avoid list and a useful proxy for late-cycle froth when issuance accelerates.
insights.quote: They do seem uniquely bad among all kind of like the menagerie of meme coins. It's like at the bottom is like celeb coins.

insights.claim: AMC's CEO publicly attacked Robinhood for tokenizing AMC stock without consent, calling it contemptible, outrageous, disgusting, detestable, inexcusable and vile, demanding a voluntary cease and desist, and arguing the tokens are a fictitious synthetic equity market decoupled from demand for the underlying stock with no capital raising, voting or registry rights.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: This is the first loud issuer-versus-tokenizer confrontation over listed US equity, and how it resolves sets the template for whether issuers get any veto over tokenization.
insights.quote: Robin Hood tokenizing their stock without their permission, without their consent, was contemptable, outrageous, disgusting, detestable, inexcusable, and vile.

insights.claim: Robinhood's chief legal officer, a former SEC commissioner, responded to AMC's complaint by inviting AMC to send its lawyers to be educated, signaling that Robinhood believes tokenizing a listed company's stock without issuer consent is plainly legal and that issuers currently have no say in the matter.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: If issuer consent is genuinely not required, tokenized-equity supply can scale against issuer objection, and the constraint becomes regulatory action rather than corporate negotiation.
insights.quote: send your lawyers and we will educate them

insights.claim: AMC's unusual sensitivity to tokenization stems from its verified-stockholder rewards and loyalty program and its history of mobilizing retail holders for governance votes, so a synthetic token that severs the registry link threatens its direct relationship with its retail shareholder base.
insights.speaker: Tom Schmidt, Dragonfly
insights.so_what: Companies with retail loyalty programs and activist shareholder bases have the most to lose from tokenization, making them the likely plaintiffs and lobbying force in this fight.
insights.quote: I think you know this guy probably saw this as oh no you're like severing this lifeline between you know me and my like horde of uh you know retail investors

insights.claim: The AMC dispute is materially different from Robinhood's earlier clash with OpenAI, because the OpenAI tokens were effectively an uncollateralized naked forward or vague SPV interest marketed as actual ownership of a private company's shares, whereas AMC involves a listed stock.
insights.speaker: Tom Schmidt, Dragonfly
insights.so_what: Distinguishing private pre-IPO synthetic exposure from public-equity tokenization matters because the two face very different disclosure and enforcement risks.

insights.claim: AMC previously attempted its own stock rewards program and could not convert its retail hype into a first-party product, and it used a prior retail mania to execute a large at-the-money share issuance, so the real objection to tokenization may be loss of control over the timing of its own share distribution.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra, Gauntlet
insights.so_what: Reading the issuer's objection as a fight over who monetizes retail enthusiasm, rather than over investor protection, changes what a negotiated settlement would look like.
insights.quote: they want control over that because then they know when to dump their shares because like last time this happened they did an at the money issuance.

insights.claim: The strongest issuer-side argument, attributed to Backpack's Armani, is that widely held synthetic debt-like equity instruments impair a company's ability to raise capital in public markets, and the fix is one-to-one backed tokenization with a mint and redeem model, which is expected to be solved within five years.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: Fully backed mint-and-redeem tokenized equity is the structure that could get issuer buy-in, so watch for infrastructure providers building it rather than synthetic exposure venues.
insights.quote: if you can move to a model that actually is onetoone backed with a mint redeem model and it actually is the actual representation of the equity then you can actually do this much better

insights.claim: The claim that synthetic tokenized stock diverts demand from the underlying is weak, because whoever issues that synthetic exposure hedges by holding the underlying, so buying the derivative still pushes up the spot price.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: This undercuts the core economic complaint from issuers and suggests tokenization is demand-additive to spot, not demand-substituting, absent evidence of naked exposure.
insights.quote: If you buy a derivative, you also push up the spot price because whoever's selling you the derivative is hedging it.

insights.claim: Shareholder communication is bifurcating into a machine-readable document dump consumed instantly by AI agents at trading firms and hedge funds, and a separate entertainment-format stream for retail vibe traders, which will make the traditional earnings conference call an artifact with no remaining audience.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Investor relations budgets, financial media formats and sell-side call access all reprice if the middle of the communication market disappears; the transition is observable in call format changes today.
insights.quote: there's like okay a document dump for the agents and that's like for all the trading firms and the hedge funds and and anybody who's like doing really sophisticated trading

insights.claim: Many earnings calls now explicitly reserve 10 to 20% of the time for non-institutional questions, a change that only occurred in the last two years and did not happen even during the GameStop mania.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra, Gauntlet
insights.so_what: Formal retail access on earnings calls is a measurable structural shift in how price-moving information gets distributed and rewards those who monitor retail-facing channels.
insights.quote: a lot of calls now have like explicit time for like non institutional questions right like they reserve 10% 20% of calls for anyone can dial in

insights.claim: Onchain issuance lets public-market participants reach private-market returns earlier through pre-IPO perpetuals on venues like Hyperliquid and prediction markets on IPO pricing, and perpetuals proved more robust than tokenized private equity because a perp needs no transfer of the underlying, as shown when Anthropic barred secondary transfers and the tokenized private equity positions went to nothing while the perps were unaffected.
insights.speaker: Paul, co-founder of FOMO
insights.so_what: Cash-settled derivatives are the durable way to get exposure to restricted private assets, and any product that depends on actual share transfer carries issuer-veto risk that can zero it.
insights.quote: anthropic said you can't trade these secondaries and then all of them went to to to nothing but the the per was fine right because the per you're just betting on a price so you actually don't need the underlying to to transfer

themes.theme: AI Math Race and Research Credit

insights.claim: OpenAI has claimed a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem, one of the Clay Millennium Prize problems, after starting work around September 3rd on hearing rumors that Anthropic had already solved it, and spent roughly $15 million of compute using an unreleased model stronger than Astra.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: A publicly disclosed $15M compute spend on a single proof gives a concrete unit-economics datapoint for frontier-model research spending and for how labs are spending on prestige benchmarks.
insights.quote: OpenAI apparently spent about $15 million worth of compute on trying to solve this problem.

insights.claim: The dispute escalated after OpenAI allegedly offered the collaborating researcher Buckmaster the Millennium Prize credit as the closest human to the solution if he disavowed his Anthropic co-researcher, which he refused before going public, and OpenAI stated it cannot rule out having trained on information the researchers fed into Codex during the period they worked on the paper.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: An admission that lab training data may include users' in-progress research is a live confidentiality risk for anyone using frontier coding tools on proprietary work.
insights.quote: we cannot rule out that we did not train on some of the information that they uh uh you know gave into into codeex during the time they worked on the paper.

insights.claim: The core mathematical idea came from two Spanish mathematicians, Diego Cordoba and Luis Martinez-Zoroa, who solved the case for low-viscosity fluids; Anthropic's result generalized it to almost all viscosities and OpenAI's covers any fluid, meaning the AI contribution was aggressive generalization search rather than a novel solution path.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra, Gauntlet
insights.so_what: The realistic near-term capability is extending known human results across parameter space, which is a very different investment case from AI originating new mathematics.
insights.quote: humans found the answer. They just didn't realize the same solution generalized. And then the AI was like we're going to search and like generalize as much as possible.

insights.claim: Academic mathematics is expected to compress into a humanities-like structure with a very small number of tenured researchers while most of the field teaches service courses, because career hierarchy was built on solving exactly the problems compute can now attack.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra, Gauntlet
insights.so_what: If elite technical research careers deflate, the talent flow and the university funding model that supports them are both exposed, with knock-on effects for research-dependent sectors.
insights.quote: everyone I know in academia is very depressed right because it's like everyone's like your your career hierarchy was determined on like trying to solve these problems but now it's kind of like actually just have more compute

insights.claim: Framing the $15 million compute spend against the $1 million Millennium Prize misses the point, because the only prior winner of the prize turned down the money and the real prize is status and proving machines can beat humans.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra, Gauntlet
insights.so_what: Prestige benchmarks, not prize money, drive frontier lab spending, so expect further uneconomic compute burns aimed at headline scientific claims.
insights.quote: All I know is there's just a very big war going on over this. And uh I think like all the people who are like, "Oh, the million-dollar prize. I spent 15 million to compute." Come on, that's idiotic.

insights.claim: The priority fight over the Navier-Stokes proof mirrors the trench trading dynamic, in that both are contests over being first to a discovery rather than over the payoff itself.
insights.speaker: Tarun Chitra, Gauntlet
insights.so_what: Status-seeking is the common driver behind both AI research races and speculative token creation, which implies neither responds much to normal economic disincentives.
insights.quote: academia is all about credit, right? It's like, oh, like who gets credit for being the first to invent this thing?
